sections.label: Mental health prevalence estimates
sections.summary: WHO estimates one-fifth of the world's population suffer mental health issues, while Singapore has one in seven adults.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: According to the WHO, it is estimated that one-fifth of the world’s population suffer from mental health issues at some point of their lives.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: In Singapore, it is one in seven adults.

sections.label: Four strategies beyond awareness
sections.summary: The speaker says awareness is not enough and offers four strategies: literacy, accessibility, screening and time-outs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Campaigns are good and platforms to share experience is great.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: However, I believe it is equally important that we go beyond awareness and I offer four strategies: literacy, accessibility, screening and time-outs.

sections.label: Regular screening strategy
sections.summary: The speaker says current touch-points may not be enough and proposes regular mental health screening for all.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: With 20 polyclinics and over 1,700 GP clinics in Singapore, but only 14 polyclinics and about 200 GPs in the programme right now, the touch-points currently may not be enough.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The third strategy is to provide regular screening just like how we do our physical health screening.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Providing regular screening for all would encourage a new norm and a behavioural change that increases acceptance and the importance of mental health.

sections.label: Literacy, accessibility, screening strategies
sections.summary: The speaker describes literacy, accessibility and screening as strategies for mental health in schools, workplaces and community touch-points.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: L for Literacy – as we push forward for mental health and social media literacy in schools and workplaces.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: A for Accessibility – as we increase the number of community touch-points and make it easier for them to come forward to seek help.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: S for Screening – to provide regular mental health screening for all Singaporeans.

sections.label: AIC community outreach teams
sections.summary: By end 2019, AIC set up 43 community outreach teams reaching over 300,000 persons and assisting over 23,000 at risk.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: As of end 2019, AIC has set up 43 community outreach teams which reached out to more than 300,000 persons and assisted over 23,000 people at risk of developing mental health conditions or dementia.

sections.label: Hotline call volume
sections.summary: The hotline has since managed over 30,000 calls.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: The hotline has since managed over 30,000 calls.

sections.label: Network preliminary initiatives mental health
sections.summary: The Network identified 15 preliminary initiatives in eight broad areas, including mental health literacy, reducing stigma and building emotional resilience.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Their diverse views and insights have enhanced our collective understanding and the Network has since identified 15 preliminary initiatives, within eight broad areas of interest, and these include enhancing mental health literacy, reducing stigma, and building emotional resilience.

sections.label: Taskforce identifying mental health issues
sections.summary: The Taskforce will be better placed to identify issues and conduct deep dives to better address collective mental health needs.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: In fact, the Taskforce will be better placed to identify issues such as those raised by the hon Member, Dr Wan Rizal, and conduct deep dives so that our people's collective mental health needs could be better addressed.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: We look forward to journeying with both the Taskforce and the Network to evolve the mental health and well-being landscape in Singapore.
